rationale_code: `AI_TUTOR_TOOL` only reads a static markdown resource shipped inside the CLI package (`../resources/ai-tutor.md`) and returns it. No user data, no network egress, no execution. The content is package-bundled and therefore public, so it is neither SECRET nor attacker-controllable.

`createBestPracticesHandler` either returns the CLI-bundled `best-practices.md` (`getBundledBestPractices`) or a markdown file referenced by `angular.bestPractices.path` inside the resolved `@angular/core` package. The read is pinned to the installed package directory: `relative`/`isAbsolute` traver

The handler sends `query` only to the fixed Algolia application `ALGOLIA_APP_ID` index `angular_v<version>` (doc-search.js:298-322), which is a fixed vendor endpoint and therefore not a SINK; the agent cannot choose the destination. Content fetching is gated on `url.hostname === 'angular.dev' || url

The handler opens SQLite files on the host and returns rows into the agent context: the bundled `exampleDatabasePath`, databases discovered from the caller-supplied `input.workspacePath` via `getVersionSpecificExampleDatabases`, or an arbitrary directory named by `NG_MCP_EXAMPLES_DIR` through `setup

`createListProjectsHandler` walks the client roots (or `process.cwd()` when the client has no roots capability, projects.js:461-467) with `findAngularJsonFiles`, loads every `angular.json` via `AngularWorkspace.load`, and returns local paths, project names, builders, source roots and `@angular/core`

`fileOrDirPath` is an unconstrained absolute path: `statSync` then `glob(`${fileOrDirPath}/**/*.ts`)` enumerates the tree and `createSourceFile` reads each file's full text (`sourceFile.getFullText()`, line 156).
